title: AttenPIM: Accelerating LLM Attention with Dual-mode GEMV in Processing-in-Memory
problem: Attention computations in LLMs are memory-bound; PIM offloading ignores dynamic matrix dimensions (token-length-dependent) and distinct patterns between score ($Q \times K_t$) and context ($S \times V$) GEMVs, leading to inefficient uniform processing.
motivation: LLM attention dominates inference latency and energy; PIM offers promise but requires specialized handling of dynamic GEMV dimensions and asymmetric computation patterns.
method: AttenPIM: dual-mode PIM computing tailored for score vs context computations; bank-level execution with configurable per-bank PIM units; PIM-oriented data layouts for KV storage; token-level and head-level concurrency for workload balance; dynamic allocation and kernel fusion.
key_novelty: First dual-mode PIM architecture recognizing distinct GEMV patterns and dynamic dimensions in LLM attention.
contributions: Dual-mode computing for score and context GEMV operations
Configurable per-bank PIM units with dynamic execution flows
Token-level and head-level parallelism for workload balancing
Dynamic memory allocation and kernel fusion optimizations
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific LLM models and sequence lengths; scalability to very long contexts and sparse attention not explored.
primary_theme: Dual-mode PIM architecture for asymmetric LLM attention GEMV
